brief.title: Check argument type in expanded-record regression test functions
brief.problem: The regression test functions expanded_record_info(), expanded_record_identity() and expanded_record_field_text() take a polymorphic argument, so a scalar such as an integer passes function resolution. They then treat the Datum as a pointer to an expanded record, so `SELECT expanded_record_info(2);` in the regression database crashes the backend. SQLsmith found the crash on current master.
brief.proposed_design: Before converting the Datum, each of the three C functions checks that the resolved argument type is a row type. The change touches only src/test/regress/regress.c.
user_visible_surface: expanded_record_info(), expanded_record_identity() and expanded_record_field_text() in the regression database now reject non-row arguments instead of crashing.
author_claims: SQLsmith on current master found a query that crashes the backend.
After the regression tests run, `SELECT expanded_record_info(2);` reproduces the crash.
The same flaw exists in expanded_record_identity() and expanded_record_field_text().

precedents_retrieved.title: Mark function arguments of type "T *" as "const T *" where possible
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds const to pointer parameters of functions, mostly static ones, that do not modify the pointed-to data, the same idea as commit 8a27d418f8f for all pointer types. A coccinelle script generated the changes, and v2 touched 251 files.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Jacob Champion argued that the patch is too large to review and that it was built by removing known-bad cases, so the const additions lack intent. He gave InitializeLDAPConnection(const Port *) as an example where const would stop future code from writing to a context struct. The author agreed and planned smaller patches limited to copy, cmp, check and size functions. The entry was then withdrawn, and the thread does not show a new version.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Especially knowing that the patchset was formed via subtraction of
known-bad cases rather than addition of known-good cases. `const`
needs to be added with intent.

precedents_retrieved.title: calculate and use most common type for polymorphic arguments
precedents_retrieved.summary: Polymorphic functions with several anyelement or anyarray arguments would resolve a common type for those arguments with the UNION rules (select_common_type), the way COALESCE does. Calls such as foo(1, 1.1) or a VARIADIC anyarray call with mixed integer and numeric values would then work without explicit casts.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said the change makes type resolution less predictable and adds more ways to match a call, so it raises the risk of "ambiguous function call" errors. He also said implicit promotion gives surprising results: appending a float to an integer array would turn the whole array into float, and anyrange cases could be worse. Heikki Linnakangas confirmed with the patch that array_append(int[], float) returns double precision[], agreed that this behaviour change is not wanted, and marked the entry rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
An example of what would presumably happen if we adopted this sort of rule
(I've not checked whether the patch as written does this, but it would
logically follow) is that appending a float to an integer array would
cause the whole array to be silently promoted to float, with attendant
possible loss of precision for existing array elements.  That does not
seem to me to satisfy the principle of least astonishment.

precedents_retrieved.title: Test for function error in logrep worker
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a TAP test to src/test/subscription/t/100_bugs.pl for a logical replication apply worker that hit a failed Assert in pg_proc.c when a function called from a subscriber trigger raised an error. The test runs an insert on the publisher and checks that the subscriber logs the expected error instead of crashing.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the case did not justify a permanent test. The crash came from a speculative Assert that had already been removed, and he saw no need for a test to stop it from coming back. He said that adding tests of this kind makes the suite slow enough that developers cannot run it easily. The author withdrew the entry after this reply.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I don't think we need a test
case to keep us from putting back the Assert.  That line of thinking
leads to test suites that run for fourteen hours and are near useless
because developers can't run them easily.

precedents_retrieved.title: change regexp_substr first argument make tests more easier to understand
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the input string in the regexp_substr() regression tests in strings.sql from 'abcabcabc' to 'abcaXcaYc', so each match returns a different substring. A later version also changed the regexp_instr() tests the same way.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane argued that these tests exist to show the functions' behavior with several copies of the target substring. With distinct substrings, a correct result could also come from the pattern failing to match elsewhere, so the change weakens the tests. Tomas Vondra had earlier asked whether the change made the tests weaker. The entry was then withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Thus, what Jian is proposing breaks the
tests: it's no longer perfectly clear whether the result is because
the function did what we expect, or because the pattern failed to
match anywhere else.

precedents_retrieved.title: allow mix of composite and scalar variables in target list
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch removes the PL/pgSQL parser check that rejects a row (composite) variable inside a multiple-item INTO list. With several targets, each target would take one output column, so a composite variable would receive one composite-valued column; record variables were left out.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that this makes a row variable mean one column in a multi-item INTO list but one column per field when it is the only target. That inconsistency would also limit later changes for backward-compatibility reasons. He asked for new notation that removes the ambiguity, and Robert Haas's support for the 1:1 matching did not settle it. The CF manager moved the patch on as needing a revised version, and Pavel Stehule answered with two new design options.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm fine with doing something where we add new notation to dispel
the ambiguity.  I don't want to put in another layer of inconsistency
and then have even more backwards-compatibility problems constraining
our response to the inevitable complaints.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reword docs of GUCs restart_after_crash and remove_temp_files_after_crash
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch rewords the docs and guc.c descriptions of restart_after_crash and remove_temp_files_after_crash, which say "backend crash". The new text lists the processes whose crash triggers the behaviour: backends, auxiliary processes except startup, syslogger and stats collector, and background workers.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas objected that the docs would then repeat the same list of exceptions every time they mention a crash. He suggested documenting in one central place which conditions start a crash-and-restart cycle. Daniel Gustafsson accepted this and proposed closing the entry as rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It seems to me that it will result in a lot of
duplication in the docs, because every time we talk about something
that happens in connection with a crash, we'll need to talk about this
same list of exceptions.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add test module for verifying backtrace functionality
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds TAP tests that check the backtrace code in elog.c (backtrace_functions, backtrace_on_internal_error, errbacktrace) by looking for "BACKTRACE: " and the failing function name in the server log. It first used a new module, src/test/modules/test_backtrace, and later moved the test to src/test/modules/test_misc.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut noted that backtrace_on_internal_error had been removed, so the patch needed changes, and suggested joining a separate thread about its replacement. The thread shows no reply or new version after that, and the entry was withdrawn. The visible messages do not show why it was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Note that backtrace_on_internal_error has been removed, so this patch
will need to be adjusted for that.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add more TAP coverage for archive status with crash recovery of standbys
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Add more TAP coverage for archive status with crash recovery of standbys
Reverted commit(s): Remove some unstable parts from new TAP test for archive status check
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This part of the test was included originally in 4e87c48, but got
reverted as of f9c1b8d because of timing issues in the test, where,
after more analysis, we found that the standbys may not have recovered
from the archives all the segments needed by the test.  This stabilizes
the test by making sure that standbys replay up to the position returned
by pg_switch_wal(), meaning that all segments are recovered before the
manual checkpoint that tests WAL segment recycling and its interactions
with archive status files.

precedents_retrieved.title: Upper limit arguments of pg_logical_slot_xxx_changes functions accept invalid values
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_logical_slot_get_changes_guts() set upto_nchanges to 0 instead of InvalidXLogRecPtr when the argument is NULL. It also rejects negative upto_nchanges values and invalid upto_lsn values with an error.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier noted that a negative upto_nchanges can reasonably mean unlimited, and the author then offered to fix only the InvalidXLogRecPtr assignment. Robert Haas argued that the current code is no less robust than the proposed form and should stay as it is. Michael Paquier closed the entry because the existing behavior has been in place for several releases.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I am not prepared to spend much time arguing about it, but I think we
should just leave this the way it is.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert addition of third argument to format_type().
precedents_retrieved.summary: Revert addition of third argument to format_type().
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Including collation in the behavior of that function promotes a world view
we do not want.  Moreover, it was producing the wrong behavior for pg_dump
anyway: what we want is to dump a COLLATE clause on attributes whose
attcollation is different from the underlying type, and likewise for
domains, and the function cannot do that for us.  Doing it the hard way
in pg_dump is a bit more tedious but produces more correct output.

In passing, fix initdb so that the initial entry in pg_collation is
properly pinned.  It was droppable before :-(

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P3] shares only the theme of regression-test crashes: it was a withdrawn proposal to add a permanent TAP test for an already-removed Assert, while this patch adds argument checks to three test functions in regress.c and is not shown to add a test. From the prior-attempts angle there is nothing to object to. Not checked without the code: the error message, whether other regress.c functions have the same flaw, and back-branch scope.

From the standards and compatibility angle there is nothing to object to. The patch changes only C test functions in src/test/regress/regress.c, which exist only in the regression database. It adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object, pg_dump or psql surface, and no client-visible behaviour beyond replacing a crash with an error. P3 concerns adding a permanent test and does not apply to this fix.

The patch changes only argument checks in regression test functions in src/test/regress/regress.c. It has no on-disk, WAL, replication, catalog, wire-protocol or extension-ABI state, so this angle has nothing to object to.

The functions exist only in the regression database, built from regress.c, and are never installed in a production cluster. The patch adds an argument check and grants no new privilege or exposure, so there is no security angle to object to.

The patch adds argument checks to three test-only C functions in src/test/regress/regress.c. It adds no per-query cost, no catalog or API surface, and nothing for users outside the regression database, so the maintenance cost is near zero. [P3] does not apply because that thread was about adding a permanent test, and this patch fixes a crash. The material does not show whether other functions in regress.c have the same flaw.

Postgres has no existing feature, contrib module or extension that stops these regress.c test functions from crashing on a scalar argument. Narrowing the SQL declaration to a row type would change test behaviour, and the proposal uses the usual type check, so it adds no duplicate mechanism. [P3] is about adding a test and does not apply to a crash fix.

The demand angle has no objection. The users are developers and fuzzers such as SQLsmith that run in the regression database, and message #1 shows a reproducible crash. The fix changes only src/test/regress/regress.c, so it adds nothing to user surface, catalogs or hot paths. [P3] is about adding a permanent test for a removed Assert, so its reason does not apply to a crash fix in test code.
